Lamp base is made with a nickel plated cast iron base plate and solid brass top estimated to be between 90 to 110 years old. No shade was on it when found, so a shade was chosen out of older stock. This custom lamp shade was re-made by hand and was done in 1990 by a professional seamstress from an old frame that was needing to be redone. The original lamp shade was made in the 1940’s and had to be completely redone. A newer cord has been added along with NEW lamp socket insert replacement as well. Lamp comes with two new super cool LED light bulb and it is advised to always use a very cool lamp as to keep the shade coloring intact for many years. listings.description: This lamp was purchased at an estate sale in 1973 and has been in storage until now. Picked up in the Cherry Creek neighborhood from a large corner mansion that had belonged to a lamp maker and designer with well over 600 lights in the house. As back stock for my mom's antique store, it would have been nice to get this sold long ago. However, mom is 85 and closed Foxy’s antiques in 2005, so this unit has to go. Base is solid glass and has gold plating on top and bottom as pictures show. Lamp is estimated to be between around 60 years to 70 old. As no shade was found on this lamp, one was used out of back stock. This custom lamp shade was re-made by hand and was done in 1998 by a professional seamstress from an old frame that was needing to be redone. The original lamp shade was made in the 1940’s and had to be completely redone. No other offers are being accepted at this time. Local pickup and Cash only for this item can be accepted. This item is being sold AS-IS and cannot be returned. If this item is listed, it is still available.

listings.description: I have a Vintage Craftsman 3-1/2" Swivel Base Bench Vise No. 506-51801 with Pipe Jaws and Anvil that is in excellent condition. The No. 506-51801 is a highly sought-after, USA-made vise manufactured for Sears by Columbian from the 1950s through the 1980s. Built for durability and dependability, this American-made vise is constructed from 30,000 psi cast iron. The replaceable micro-grooved steel jaws have a strong grip and will prevent objects from moving around once you clamp them in place. The built-in fixed cast iron pipe jaws are grooved for enhanced grip and allow for easy clamping of pipe and other rounded material. An anvil work surface on the back of the vise is perfect for hammering and shaping metal pieces. The 210° swivel base allows this vise to be positioned so work pieces can be clamped with ease. The machine steel main screw with rolled threads is wear-resistance which provides smooth operation. Whether you are working with wood or metal at home or in the shop, this 3-1/2" heavy-duty workshop bench vise provides 4,000 lbs. clamping force and holding power needed to get the job done with confidence. Jaws open to 4-1/2". Weighs 15.6 lbs. Rust-free with original, iconic Craftsman red paint still very much in evidence. Includes mounting bolts, nuts and washers. If you are an early Craftsman aficionado, then this is a must-have. $80 NOTE: The cast-in arrowhead symbol next to the model number under base indicates that the part originated from a high-quality, specialized iron forge. The small number cast directly inside the arrowhead was used by the foundry workers for quality control and mold tracking. PLEASE INCLUDE YOUR TELEPHONE NUMBER WHEN INQUIRING. THE PROLIFERATION OF BOGUS INQUIRIES ON CRAIGSLIST THESE DAYS NECESSITATE THIS REQUEST.

listings.description: Title: Out of Pod Experience I, II, III Medium: Acrylic on canvas Dimensions: Triptych; each panel 12 × 12 in; integrated bare wood frame Out of Pod Experience is a modernist triptych that explores perception beyond containment—an abstract meditation on emergence, continuity, and shared fields of awareness. Across the three panels, undulating bands of saturated color form interconnected pathways, punctuated by concentric nodes that suggest energy centers, cellular structures, or points of resonance. The repeated motifs—rings, ripples, and flowing lines—create a visual language that moves laterally across the triptych, encouraging the viewer to read the work as a single, continuous experience rather than discrete moments. Vibrant reds, blues, yellows, and greens pulse against one another, evoking both biological systems and topographical maps of sensation. The work balances playfulness with intention, grounding its psychedelic palette in disciplined repetition and modernist structure. Out of Pod Experience I Repeated bands and concentric forms initiate a shift from enclosure toward open spatial continuity. Out of Pod Experience II Rhythmic pathways and recurring nodes establish lateral movement across a shared visual field. Out of Pod Experience III Flow resolves into a sustained pattern, emphasizing continuity over containment.

listings.description: I have a Vintage (1931 - 1947*) 16-Piece Craftsman 1/4" Drive SAE Mechanics Socket Set that is in excellent condition. Included are 11 (6, 8 and 12-point) sockets ranging from 5/32" to 1/2" with only the 5/32", 3/16", 3/8" and 1/2" representing the modern era inverted "G" series. Also included are a flex-head (hinge) breaker bar with 4" 'cheater bar', 5" T-handle, 3" extension and metal case (6"L x 1-3/4"W x 1"H) with original paint and a discernible 'Craftsman Tools' label. The majority of pieces are the knurled -BE- Series with underlined C Circle H Logo from the 1940's. No owner's marks. Made in Kenosha, WI U.S.A.🇺🇸 $60 * SOURCE: garagejournal.com Also, I have a rare Craftsman "BE" Series 1/4" drive, open head ratchet that is in excellent condition. Dating back to the 1930's, the ratchet is 5-1/4" long and has a chrome plating finish with the Craftsman underline logo and a "BE" code on the top cover plate. The design for the 1/4" drive model was an open-style reversible ratchet with riveted construction instead of the forged-body construction used previously for both 1/4" and 3/8" drive stamped versions. The ratchet is reversible by rotating the pawl to work on the other side, and the side edges of the pawl are serrated to provide a grip. The pawl bias is maintained by a spring-loaded ball carried in the pawl itself rather than in the handle shaft. The handle shaft has a knurled grip best suited for slippery, greasy, and wet environments. Made in the U.S.A. for Sears/Craftsman by the the New Britain (CT.) Machine Company. A great piece for the die-hard Craftsman collector! $50 or buy both the socket set and ratchet for $110. Information Source: alloy-artifacts.org PLEASE INCLUDE YOUR TELEPHONE NUMBER WHEN INQUIRING.

listings.description: I have two vintage Craftsman flat slot screwdrivers. The first is No.41585 WF 1/4" x 12" square shaft with an overall tool length of 16". The second is No.41588 WF 3/8" x 13" square shaft with an overall tool length of 17". Both are in like-new condition. Made in the U.S.A.🇺🇸 $25 each or buy them both for $40. NOTE: The initials WF stand for Western Forge. Western Forge was an American manufacturing company established in 1965 to produce high-quality hand tools for Sears, specifically under the Craftsman brand. They opened a forging plant in Colorado Springs, Colorado, in 1966 and were known for being the largest American manufacturer of screwdrivers. They were a major supplier of US-made Craftsman tools from 1965 until April 2017, when the company lost its contract with Sears. SOURCE: alloy-artifacts.org PLEASE INCLUDE YOUR TELEPHONE NUMBER WHEN INQUIRING.

little about me In 1959 I learned to drive off-road at 6 years old. In early 1961 Clarence (my dad), and 3 of his friends created the Trailblazer . Our Class 1 Structural Fill Dirt is $18.95 per ton, 1 ton covers 100 square feet ( 10 feet wide by 10 feet long) 2 inches deep. The pictures posted are the most recent pictures we have of the material, we do not guarantee the color, but everyone who has purchased it is very happy with it. You can buy with confidence and know if we recommend a specific material for your project, that is the best material to use, whether you purchase it from us or not. We often talk with people who tried the least expensive option(cheap fill dirt from a construction site), received a load of dirt with clods the size of a large pumpkin and spent twice as much time and work completing their project. Class 1 Structural Fill in a fine material that is easy to work with whether you are using a shovel or a machine. Our goal (and yours) should be to get the best material for your project, in the correct amount, the first time, get the job done and get back to the rest of your life. Our trucks can hold up to 15 tons, we have an 8 ton minimum delivery. This bike is designed for riders who enjoy exploring the road less traveled. Its robust Columbus steel frame provides durability and a smooth ride, while the dedicated carbon fork helps absorb vibrations, making those bumpy paths feel more manageable. The Hook EXT is built to take on gravel paths, dirt trails, and everything in between—making it a great choice for ambitious riders who want to tackle diverse terrains. One of the standout features of the Hook EXT is its 27.5’’ wheelset. This size strikes a perfect balance between stability and agility, ensuring you can navigate tight turns and unpredictable surfaces with confidence. The WTB ST Light double-wall rims, coupled with tubeless-ready WTB Ranger tires, provide excellent traction and reduce the risk of pinch flats, allowing you to ride longer distances without the worry of frequent repairs. The SRAM 1x11 Rival groupset is another impressive component of this gravel bike. Thanks to its single chainring setup, you're offered a streamlined design that simplifies gear shifting without sacrificing performance or versatility. Plus, the SRAM RIVAL flat mount hydraulic disc brakes, equipped with 160 mm rotors, offer powerful stopping power in all conditions, ensuring safety on downhill stretches or during unpredictable weather. The ergonomics of the Hook EXT make it a joy to ride. With internal light cable routing and a rear light mount, you can easily add lighting to your setup for those early morning or late evening excursions. The 86.5 mm T47 BB shell enhances the bike's stiffness and response, giving you that extra confidence when pushing through challenging routes. Riders will appreciate the practicality that comes with the triple cage mounts on the carbon fork, which also double as fender mounts. This means you can equip the bike with racks or fenders for long trips or inclement weather without hassle, making it a versatile choice for serious cyclists. Whether you're carrying gear for a weekend adventure or adding fenders for wet weather protection, the Hook EXT accommodates your needs. Riders and reviewers alike have praised the Bombtrack Hook EXT for its sturdy build, responsiveness, and comfort. Many highlight how well it handles in diverse conditions, making it a great companion for both gravel rides and daily commuting. If you enjoy pushing your limits and exploring the outdoors, the Bombtrack Hook EXT is the gravel bike tailored for you. It's a perfect mix of modern technology and rugged design, crafted for those who relish every ride, wherever the path may lead.

listings.description: Duluth Trading Co Master Series Black Fire Hose Tact Squad Auto Tool Organizer A Lady asked an old street vendor: "How much do you sell your eggs for?" The old man replied "0.50¢ an egg, madam.” The Lady responded, “I'll take 6 eggs for $2.00 or I'm leaving.” The old salesman replied, “Buy them at the price you want, Madam. This is a good start for me because I haven't sold a single egg today and I need this to live.” She bought her eggs at a bargain price and left with the feeling that she had won. She got into her fancy car and went to a fancy restaurant with her friend. She and her friend ordered what they wanted. They ate a little and left a lot of what they had asked for. So they paid the bill, which was $150. The ladies gave $200 and told the fancy restaurant owner to keep the change as a tip. This story might seem quite normal to the owner of the fancy restaurant, but very unfair to the egg seller. The question it raises is; Why do we always need to show that we have power when we buy from the needy? And why are we generous to those who don't even need our generosity? We once read somewhere that a father used to buy goods from poor people at a high price, even though he didn't need the things. Sometimes he paid more for them. His children were amazed. One day they asked him "why are you doing this dad?" The father replied: "It's charity wrapped in dignity.” I know that most of you will not share this message, but if you are one of the people who have taken the time to read this far... Then this message of attempted "humanization" will have gone one step further in the right direction.

listings.description: Rene Couturier French artist – 1950’s – huge bright postwar piece from French Normandy region. Very well auctioned artist. I'll post actual dimensions shortly. Originally purchased at a hospital auction in San Francsico where the piece was originally displayed back in the 90s. A true museum piece where the value will continue to rise as you enjoy over the years. Rene Couturier is a world renowned artist whose works display a master virtuosity. His talent encompasses the bold figurative lines of the “Jeune Painture” Movement, the power of an Abstract dimension, and a phenomenal color technique which is distinctly his own. Couturier’s super-imposed layers of sand and oil paint are blended on canvas by pallete knife. From this textured foundation his brilliant tones are brought forth with an astounding intensity. The resulting composition is a vigorous contrast of color on texture, texture on dimension. Born in 1933 in Dieppe, Normandy, a coastal town in France, Rene Couturier began drawing before he could walk. His artistic ambitions withstood four adolescent years at a watchmaking school and he later went on to study l’Ecole des Beaux of Marseille. From 1958 to 1968 he was represented in several group and salon shows of France. Couturier has since embarked on a round of exhibitions throughout Europe, Africa, Canada and the United States. Several of Couturier’s landscapes and still-life paintings were inspired by his native seaside environment. Many others are culled from far reaching sojourns to Brazil, Morocco, Spain and Mali, and six months on the Ivory Coast. Often likened to Bernard Buffet, Rene Couturier’s works reflect a similar eye for subject studies, but the focus of their intent originates from a uniquely personal source of fervor. Couturier’s remarkable talent stands apart as enlightened testimony: his art is self-evident.

The result is a smoother, friction-free feeling of pure forward momentum. To reduce drag even more, M-pulse hubs offer preload adjustment, allowing the bearings to spin as smooth as possible. Alloy-Artifacts.org: The Walworth Manufacturing Company was founded by James J. Walworth as a maker of plumbing pipes and equipment in Boston, Massachusetts. The company began in 1852 as J.J. Walworth & Company and later incorporated as the Walworth Manufacturing Company in 1872. The founder served served as company president until 1890. Walworth Manufacturing is most famous as the original maker of the Stillson pipe wrench, named after its inventor Daniel Stillson, who was an employee of the company at the time. The original Stillson design was covered by patent 95,744, filed by Daniel Stillson in 1869 and issued later that year. The Stillson pipe wrench became one of the most successful tools of all time, and royalties from the patent made a small fortune for the inventor. We could make the argument that the Stillson patent was the most important tool patent of the 19th century, based not only on the merits of the tool itself (which are considerable), but also on the inspiration and encouragement that Daniel Stillson's financial success provided for future inventors.

listings.description: Owner's Description: Little used Zuma sailing dinghy with trailer and launch dolly. All in great condition. Includes new rigging--ready to sail! AI Description: The Zuma is a 13-foot, lightweight fiberglass dinghy popular for easy day sailing. Weighing just 130 pounds, it features a simple, unstayed sail, a kick-up rudder, and a daggerboard. It is stable and forgiving, making it a great boat for beginners and families.Key Specs and Design Length: 12 feet 9 inches (12.75 ft)Beam (Width): 5 feet Weight: 129 lbs Sail Area: 65 sq ft. Why It's Great: Easy Setup: The Zuma uses a sleeve-cut sail that zips right over the mast. This means you can hoist and lower the sail without taking the mast down. Stability: Compared to similar performance boats (like the Laser), the Zuma has a flatter, more buoyant hull. This helps it stay stable and keeps the front of the boat from dipping under the waves. Portability: Because the boat is so light, one or two people can easily lift and load it onto a car roof rack or a small trailer. How it Sails: The Zuma uses a cat rig, meaning it only has one sail. It is very responsive in light winds but still fun and fast. Since it has a daggerboard (a board you drop through the boat into the water to stop it from sliding sideways) and a kick-up rudder (a steering blade that flips up if you hit bottom), it is perfect for beach launches and shallow water.
